### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39fafc0dfeed129ce7f37e444f39e04dc670aa0b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `884489963ab94dc205e38555a672d0968d5ac273` — the merge of head `048071109ffec30340d4e57df9418d46c5e50901` into base `39fafc0dfeed129ce7f37e444f39e04dc670aa0b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 884489963ab94dc205e38555a672d0968d5ac273 && git checkout 884489963ab94dc205e38555a672d0968d5ac273
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 39fafc0dfeed129ce7f37e444f39e04dc670aa0b 048071109ffec30340d4e57df9418d46c5e50901 && git checkout -B drift-repro 39fafc0dfeed129ce7f37e444f39e04dc670aa0b && git merge --no-ff 048071109ffec30340d4e57df9418d46c5e50901

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39fafc0dfeed129ce7f37e444f39e04dc670aa0b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `048071109ffec30340d4e57df9418d46c5e50901`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/disabled-holder-packageless-row-doors.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.disabled-holder-package-less-row-bare-write-refused.ts` + `.changeset/37851-disabled-holder-own-row-publish-rollback-refused.md`, `.changeset/37608-disabled-holder-publish-rollback-refused.md` (both judged sentence by sentence in ②); read, not reviewed: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-row-bindings.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts`, `docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md` on `main` 21ad7c54, `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`

Read: card #37851 and its four comments (measurement 7216513948, ruling 7216539589, claim 7217032154, os-dev report 7219375856), the PR body and both PR comments, the net diff 73d5e347..04807110 (7 files, +174 −35), and the 68 check-runs on the head as of 13:28Z. `main` is 18 commits past the merge base; none of them touches a file of this diff.

### ① Derived judgments

Every answer the diff moves, all for a type the registry reads by package, no package named, every holder of the name disabled. Each is judged against ruling A (7216539589).

- **Cell (a), bare publish of the disabled package's own draft** (`promoteDraftForPublish`, the `ownDraft` arm): `200` → `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, the `?package=` sentence (`disabledHoldersOnlyRefusal`, verb `publish`), beside a stored package-less row or with none. **Right.** It is the sentence the ruling names for (a). The remedy is correct for the cell: the promotion reads and writes the package's own draft and row only, and the publish naming the package reaches both (pinned as the control in both `it.each` rows, the package-less row byte-identical). `unbound: !ownDraft` leaves the package-less-draft arm exactly as #37818 left it (enable sentence).
- **Cell (b), bare rollback whose restore writes the package-unbound row, none stored** (`rollbackMetaItemUnaudited`, `rollbackPackageId === null`): `200` (row inserted from history) → `409`, the enable sentence (`disabledHoldersCustomizationRefusal`, verb `rollback`). **Right.** It is the sentence the ruling names for (b); naming the package would address another slot, so `?package=` is not the remedy here. The re-enable control restores the version.
- **Cell (c), bare rollback of the disabled package's own row** (`rollbackPackageId` is the package): `200` → `409`, the `?package=` sentence. **Right.** The ruling asks for a measurement first; the PR records the pin red on `main` 73d5e347 ("no refusal"), so it lands and is refused in the same PR. The rollback naming the package restores it (pinned).
- **Undeclared, same door, error to error**: the judgment now sits ahead of `repo.restoreVersion`, the only source of `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND` and `409 VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` on an unaddressed slot. So a bare rollback at such a name to a version that has no history row (including a code-shipped item with no stored row and no history at all) moves from that `404` to the `409` of cell (b) or (c). Nothing was written before or after, and at the merge base the cell with a package-less row stored already answered the `409` first, so the direction is the house order (the save and the delete also judge before the address resolves). The code is **right**; the note does not list it, see N2. The publish keeps `404 NO_DRAFT` (`address.kind === 'draft'` guards the ask), as declared.
- **Unchanged, verified in the code**: a publish or rollback naming a package (the `'packageId' in request` branch and the `request.packageId === undefined` guard are untouched; REST spreads the selector only when present); any name with one enabled holder (`packagelessHolderRefusal` returns `undefined` when any candidate or known holder is neither disabled nor a disabled holder's pair, and when the type is not read by package or the environment holds the item); the ADR-0146 D11 close and the named-base close, both still ahead of the judgment on both doors; the lock gate order.
- **Other doors**: none moves. `protocol-save.ts` changes a docblock only; the body of `packagelessHolderRefusal` is byte-identical, so the save, draft save, delete and draft discard answer as before. `publishPackageDrafts` always passes `packageId` (the listed draft's key), so the package commit takes the named branch. The restore limb of `revertCommit` does not call `rollbackMetaItemUnaudited`.
- **Pins**: the flipped :320 control, each refused cell with stored rows byte-identical, the named-write control for (a) and (c), the re-enable control for (a) and (b). For (c) the re-enable step reads the row after the named rollback; it does not send the bare rollback again after the enable (N3).

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on the PR body and on the new changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. `minor` for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec` with `!` and a BREAKING sentence matches what the diff publishes (refusals where `200` was answered; a migration entry reworded) and the level the ruling set. The ADR-0087 disposition step and the major guard on the `Check Changeset` job are green; the job log reads the new note as `not-required (already-registered)`.

`@objectstack/objectql`: the change is one test file. The package publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only, so nothing of it is released. **No changeset is owed for it.**

`.changeset/37851…`, sentence by sentence against the code: the two remedies and which refusal carries which, the three bullets (before and after), the in-process bullet, the re-enable sentence and the "Not moved" list are true at this head. Two gaps, both prose: N1 and N2.

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/37608-disabled-holder-publish-rollback-refused.md`.** Before: "a rollback of a package-bound row; two writes that still land on an item only disabled packages hold, left open for a separate decision (#37851): a publish whose draft address is the disabled package's own draft, promoted into that package's own row (beside a package-less row or not), and a rollback with no package-less row stored, which stores the package-less row again from its history;". After: "a publish whose draft address is the disabled package's own draft, a rollback of a package-bound row, and a rollback with no package-less row stored, which this note leaves open and the #37851 note in the same release refuses;". Judged against the code: the old sentence is false at this head (all three are refused); the new one is true, it names the three cells this PR closes, and the rest of that note (its own two moved answers, the enable sentence, "now carries these two") still holds. **This record confirms the correction.**

The three conditions for carrying the red:
- The source describes it: `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` and `pr-automation.yml` (route 0 and the "Past a designed red" block) name the class as red by design, and the new note says "that sentence now points here". The job is red on step 10 alone, on that one file; steps 11 to 13 are green. Holds.
- `pr-automation.yml` triggers on `pull_request` only; no `merge_group`. Holds.
- A PR comment naming the gate and the reason: **not yet met when read.** The PR body declares it and the claim comment 7219399122 names the correction, but no PR comment names `Check Changeset` / `check-empty-changeset` as the red gate and why. This record does, if it is posted on the PR; posted on the card, the seat owes one PR comment before the enqueue.

**Migration entry 19**, sentence by sentence: `surface` (the three cells added for the publish and rollback), `replacement` (the "other exception" with `?package=` and the named write going through while disabled), `reason` (the #37818 S1 sentence replaced with what the doors now do) and `acceptanceCriteria` are true at this head. The criteria's "the rollback naming no package answer the same 409" also covers the no-history case of ①. The same omission as N1 applies to the criteria's first sentence.

`Skills-docs: none`: true. No page under `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` teaches a bare per-item publish or rollback over a name only disabled packages hold; the pages that name the two routes (`content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`, `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`) describe them without that cell. The docs-drift run found no hand-written page on the changed anchors.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` 1 (the enable sentence says "the row stored for it under no package" while cell (b) has only its history): answered. The ruling names that sentence for (b), so keeping it is correct in this PR. The clause is inexact in (b) and untrue in the no-history case of ①; a wording card is the right carrier, with N2.
- Dev flag, cell (c) measured first: answered, it lands on `main` 73d5e347 and is refused here.
- Dev flag, `packageId: null` in process still takes the named branch (#37818 N1): unchanged by this diff, correct to leave.
- Dev flag, ADR-0150 D3 note wording: not in this diff, as the claim's file surface requires; the note on `main` still describes the earlier state and stays owed on the seat's ADR checklist.
- File surface: `protocol-save.ts` (docblock only) and the 37608 note are outside the claim's listed files; one is a comment, the other the declared correction. No breach of the `docs/adr/**` line.
- SQL push-down: no finding. Each door adds one keyed read of the item's active rows (`packagelessAddress`, state `active`) on every bare publish with a draft and every bare rollback, where it was read only on the package-less arm. No id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Check-runs on the head at 13:28Z, 68 runs: `Check Changeset` red (by design, above); `Test UI (13/16)` in progress, a rerun after a first-attempt red the os-dev report places at `ListView.inlineFlsNoop-6723.test.tsx` under `ui/`, outside this diff. I did not wait for it. Everything else is green or skipped, including Test Core 1 to 10, the type checks, the lint families and the queue guard.
- Dogfood battery: the os-dev report pins `04807110`, `os-verify-lock` VERDICT exit 0, Test Files 490 passed, 3 skipped (493), Tests 4144 passed, 68 skipped (4212), no failures. It opens with this head's sha and reports the full run. The CI dogfood shards were skipped on this PR, so the report is the only reading.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. ADR-0150 D3 on `main` already says a disabled package holds no name, that a name only disabled packages hold "keeps its refusal and its `?package=` remedy", and that a package-less row at such a name is the holder's customization, hidden with it and remedied by the enable. The bare save answered so; the bare publish and rollback wrote. The maintainer ruled A on the card. Nothing the spec declares for a caller is removed: every write stays reachable by naming the package or by enabling it.

Attempts to break it, by code read:
- A customization pair's row of a disabled base: the pair id is in the candidates and `disabledHoldersPair` accepts it, so it is judged as the save judges it.
- A row bound to an id that is not a disabled installed package (an orphan binding, an `app.` scope): not disabled, so the judgment declines and the answer is unchanged.
- A row-held base address on the publish: `key` and `into` are the base, the candidates still include every stored binding and every known holder, so one enabled holder keeps the old answer.
- Which sentence when both a package's row and a package-less row are stored: each door picks by the row it would write, never by what else is stored, which is the ruling's own reasoning for (a).
- Batch publish and commit revert: not reachable from the changed branches (①).

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, each fixable on the changeset alone or left as a follow-up:
- N1 (nit) — the BREAKING lead of `.changeset/37851…` scopes itself to "no package-less row is stored for it", while the own-draft publish also moved beside a stored package-less row (the flipped :320 pin). The title and the first bullet say it correctly; the lead is narrower than the truth. The entry's `acceptanceCriteria` has the same omission.
- N2 (nit) — "Every moved answer" in `.changeset/37851…` omits that a bare rollback at such a name now answers the `409` ahead of `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND` and `409 VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` (①). One sentence in the note, and the wording card of ③ for the enable sentence in that state.
- N3 (nit) — cell (c) has no bare rollback after the re-enable; the named rollback and the served read stand in for it. A follow-up pin, not a head move.

The filled brief the record above was rendered from (L1-a, isolated `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` subagent):

## Contract review brief — PR #37948 @ `048071109ffec30340d4e57df9418d46c5e50901` (card #37851)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --face narrowing` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37851: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37948: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `73d5e347f7d7c755a3e86e127228791c476485e2` (the merge base)
  · the check-runs on `048071109ffec30340d4e57df9418d46c5e50901`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the narrowing is declared of the whole PR, never of a path: the floor is EVERY path of the diff outside the
  prose faces (PATH-ONE, PATH-TWO), plus every file those hunks make a claim about, read in the cited code.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below that floor; the record's `Scope:` line lists both. No path is the lane seat's remainder.
  ④ judges the narrowing itself over that floor: lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in
  the PR are not reviewed; the published spec and the cited code are READ to judge it, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-37948/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — the narrowing itself, read against the published spec on `main`: does it take a
     declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real? A capability declared
     and not delivered is an implementation gap, implemented or retired, ⛔ never narrowed at the consumer.
     Read the spec and the cited code in the live tree, and try to break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

**`Test UI (13/16)` is red on head `04807110`, and the cause is not in this PR's diff.** It failed on the first run (job 140512339260) and again on the one re-run of failed jobs (job 140529997984). Both times the failure is the same assertion in `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.inlineFlsNoop-6723.test.tsx`, case `UNAUTHORED: the grid takes the OBJECT-SCHEMA path …`: `expected [ 'Id', 'Opportunity Name' ] to not include 'Id'`.

Why it isn't this PR's:
- The diff touches `packages/metadata-protocol`, one `packages/objectql` test, a `packages/spec` migration entry's text and two changesets. Nothing under `ui/` changes, and the test renders `ListView` over an in-file mock data source with no server.
- The same file is green (3 of 3) in `Test UI (13/16)` of the `main` push run 46001713224, on `bc173343`. No `ui/` commit lands between this run's CI base `39fafc0d` and `bc173343`.
- Locally the file passes 3 of 3 from `ui/` (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.inlineFlsNoop-6723.test.tsx`), both at this head and at this head merged with `origin/main` (merge not pushed).

What the reading suggests (not reproduced): the headers carry `Id` and leave out `Amount`. That is the inline-data path, with its FLS gate, read before the object schema took over. The case takes the first non-empty header set (`waitFor(() => expect(h.length).toBeGreaterThan(0))`), so on a slower runner it can read the render before the schema loads. `3eb778d8` (#37883, a list page draws its rows once before they paint) is on the CI base and moved that timing. A fix would be for that case to wait for the schema-path header set (for example, `waitFor` until the headers equal `['Opportunity Name']`) before asserting the mechanism. That belongs in the `ui/` lane, not in this narrowing.

`Check Changeset` is red by design on the DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/37608-disabled-holder-publish-rollback-refused.md`, as the PR body and contract record 7219552890 state.
